newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..f811d767543 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md @@ -0,0 +1,87 @@ +--- +title: Protect against telephony fraud with your own telecom provider +description: Configure provider fraud protections, destination and spending controls, secure your CYOT integration, monitor unusual activity, and respond to suspected fraud. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to prevent telephony fraud and configure appropriate protections for my CYOT integration. +--- + +# Protect against telephony fraud with your own telecom provider + + + + +With Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), SMS and voice traffic runs through your own telecom provider account. You control the fraud protections, allowed destinations, and spending limits that match your organization's traffic and risk profile. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Set up your provider's fraud and spending controls before you move production traffic to CYOT. + + + +## Shared responsibility + +| Owner | Responsibility | +|---|---| +| Microsoft | Protects code generation and validation in Microsoft Entra ID, and the handoff to your endpoint. | +| Your organization | Manages the provider account, secures the integration, and configures fraud controls. | +| Telecom provider | Delivers SMS and voice, and offers fraud, destination, and spending controls. | + + + + + +## Configure fraud protections with your provider + +Work with your provider to turn on the controls available for your account: + +- **Fraud protection:** Turn on the provider's detection for suspicious SMS and voice traffic. +- **Destination restrictions:** Allow only the countries and regions where your users are. +- **Channel restrictions:** Turn on only the channels you use. +- **Spending controls:** Set usage limits and budget alerts. +- **Notifications:** Turn on alerts for unusual activity. + +> [!NOTE] +> Controls and defaults vary by provider. Ask your provider which protections are on by default and which you need to configure. + + + +## Keep your integration secure + +The setup script configures authentication and request validation for your Azure Function. Keep these settings in place, including when you customize the Function. + +Your organization is responsible for renewing and rotating the integration's application credentials and certificates. + +## Monitor for unusual activity + +Review SMS and voice volume in your provider's usage reports. A sudden increase in volume, or traffic to destinations you don't expect, can signal fraud. + + + + +## Respond to suspected fraud + +1. Contact your telecom provider to review the affected traffic. +1. Restrict the affected destinations, channels, or usage with your provider's controls. +1. Investigate the requests using the Microsoft Entra audit logs, the Function App logs, and your provider's records. +1. Update your protections before you restore traffic. + + + +## Get support + +| Issue | Contact | +|---|---| +| Fraud, provider account restrictions, delivery, or charges | Your telecom provider. Find contact details in the provider's [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/) listing. | +| Microsoft Entra authentication, code validation, or the handoff to your endpoint | Microsoft Support. See [Find help and get support for Microsoft Entra](/entra/fundamentals/how-to-get-support). | + + + +## Related content + +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [Plan for resiliency and high availability](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md). +- [Estimate telecom provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost). +- [Security Store](/security/store/what-is-security-store).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..5f22e0de234 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md @@ -0,0 +1,110 @@ +--- +title: Plan for resiliency and high availability +description: Plan CYOT resiliency with multi-region Azure Functions, Azure Front Door, a secondary telecom provider, and failover and recovery testing. +ms.topic: concept-article +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to plan and test regional and telecom provider resiliency for my CYOT integration. +--- + +# Plan for resiliency and high availability + + + + +SMS and voice authentication sit on the critical path to your applications. When users rely on a phone code for multifactor authentication (MFA) or self-service password reset (SSPR), the availability of that code determines whether they can sign in. + +With Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), the delivery path includes components your organization owns: the Azure Function in your subscription and your telecom provider. Design these components for resiliency so authentication stays available through regional outages and provider incidents. + + + +## Understand your delivery path + +| Component | Managed by | What it does | +|---|---|---| +| Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft | Generates and validates the code, and sends the request to your endpoint. | +| Endpoint and Azure Function | Your organization | Receives the request in your Azure subscription and sends it to your provider. | +| Telecom provider | Your provider | Delivers the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | + +The guided setup creates one Azure Function in a single region, connected to one telecom provider. This setup works well for evaluation and many production workloads. To protect against a regional outage or a provider incident, extend it with the options in this article. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Your organization manages the availability and recovery of the Azure resources and provider integration in your subscription. Test your resiliency design before you rely on it for production authentication. + +> [!NOTE] +> The multi-region and secondary-provider designs in this article are sample-only guidance. They aren't part of the standard deployment. Your organization is responsible for validating and maintaining these customizations. + + + +## Choose a resiliency approach + +Start with your requirements: which disruptions you must withstand, how quickly authentication must recover, and the sign-in availability your organization requires. Then choose the approach that meets them. + +| Approach | Protects against | When to use it | +|---|---|---| +| Single region, one provider (default setup) | Function App instance failures within the region | Evaluation, and production workloads that can tolerate a regional outage | +| Multi-region with Azure Front Door | Regional outages | Production workloads that require authentication during a regional disruption | +| Secondary telecom provider | Provider-specific incidents | When your primary provider alone doesn't meet your availability or coverage requirements | +| Multi-region and secondary provider | Regional outages and provider incidents | Organizations with the highest availability requirements | + + + +## Deploy across multiple regions + +A multi-region deployment uses Azure Front Door to expose one endpoint backed by Function Apps in two or more regions. Microsoft Entra ID calls the Front Door endpoint, and Front Door routes each request to a healthy region. Set it up manually after you validate a single-region deployment, because the setup script in [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md) deploys one region at a time. + +When you plan a multi-region deployment: + +- **Size each region for the full workload.** If one region is unavailable, the remaining regions must handle all authentication traffic. +- Use the same code, settings, and encryption key in every region, and coordinate certificate renewal across regions. +- **Expect failover to take time.** Some requests can fail while Front Door detects an unhealthy region and shifts traffic. +- **Plan for added cost.** Each region adds its own Function App plan, storage, Key Vault, and monitoring, plus Front Door. For estimates, see [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/COST-CALCULATOR.md). +- Adding regions improves availability, not delivery speed. SMS and voice delivery time depends mostly on your provider and carriers. + +For architecture, region and capacity planning, and step-by-step setup, see [Azure Front Door multi-region deployment](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/FRONTDOOR.md). + + + + + +## Add a secondary telecom provider + +A multi-region deployment still relies on your telecom provider. Confirm that your provider's availability commitments, redundancy, and disaster recovery meet your requirements in the countries/regions you serve. + +If one provider isn't enough, you can implement fallback to a secondary provider in your Azure Function. To avoid sending a user two codes, use the secondary provider only when the primary provider confirms it didn't accept the request. Don't resend after a timeout or unknown result, because the primary provider might already have sent the code. + +For the fallback design, see [Secondary-provider design](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md). + + + + + +## Test failover and recovery + +Before production use, test your design in a nonproduction environment: + +- Take one region or provider offline, and confirm that traffic moves to the healthy one and that it handles the full workload. +- Confirm that timeouts and unknown provider results don't trigger a second send. +- Restore the failed component, and confirm that traffic returns without errors or duplicate messages. +- Confirm that users complete SMS and voice authentication after each failover and recovery, and measure recovery time against your targets. + +Evaluation mode doesn't call your provider. Repeat your tests after any change to code, routing, configuration, or your provider integration. + +To monitor each region and provider, see [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +## Related content + +- [CYOT sample documentation](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/tree/main/docs). +- [Azure Front Door multi-region deployment](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/FRONTDOOR.md). +- [Secondary-provider design](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md). +- [Reliability in Azure Functions](/azure/reliability/reliability-functions). +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [CYOT sample documentation (epp-packages-193-1)](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/tree/epp-packages-193-1/docs). +- [Optional multi-region onboarding with Azure Front Door (epp-packages-193-1)][sample-regions]. +- [Multi-provider implementation (epp-packages-193-1)][sample-fallback]. + +[sample-regions]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/docs/FRONTDOOR.md +[sample-fallback]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md b/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..3229be91ade --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md @@ -0,0 +1,277 @@ +--- +title: Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom providers +description: Deploy your telecom integration, validate evaluation mode, and gradually roll out SMS and voice delivery by using CYOT APIs. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to deploy a telecom integration and configure SMS and voice delivery through Microsoft Graph. +--- + +# Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom providers + +Use Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) to deliver SMS and voice authentication through your organization's telephony provider. With CYOT, you purchase a supported provider offer through [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/), deploy the integration in your Azure subscription, and configure Microsoft Entra to route SMS or voice authentication through your provider. + +This article walks you through the end-to-end setup, including purchasing your provider offer, deploying the integration, configuring the authentication method policy, and testing the experience before moving to production. + +## How the integration works + +CYOT uses an Azure Function in your Azure subscription to connect Microsoft Entra with your telephony provider. The Azure Function processes SMS or voice requests from Microsoft Entra and sends them to your provider for delivery. + +:::image type="content" source="media/concept-phone-providers/telephony-provider-integration-diagram.jpeg" alt-text="Diagram of the CYOT integration connecting Microsoft Entra to a telephony provider through an Azure Function in your Azure subscription."::: + +## Prerequisites + +Before you begin, prepare: + +- A Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. +- An Azure subscription with a valid payment method to host the integration and subscribe to your provider. See [Security Store purchasing prerequisites](/security/store/customers/how-to-purchase-a-saas-solution-and-deploy-a-linked-solution#prerequisites). +- [Azure Cloud Shell](/azure/cloud-shell/overview) in PowerShell mode (recommended), or PowerShell 7.0+ with Azure CLI 2.61+ for integration deployment. +- A test user with a phone number registered for SMS or voice authentication. + +## Required permissions + +Use accounts with the following permissions: + +| Task | Required access | Why it's needed | +|---|---|---| +| Create the application | Permission to register applications in the customer tenant | Lets setup create the application that securely connects Microsoft Entra to your integration. | +| Deploy Azure resources | Subscription Owner, or Contributor + Role Based Access Control Administrator at the required scope | Lets setup deploy the integration in your subscription. | +| Grant directory access during deployment | Privileged Role Administrator | Lets setup grant the directory permissions that Microsoft Entra needs to route requests to your integration. | +| Read authentication method policy | Delegated `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod` permission and a supported role, such as Authentication Policy Administrator | Allows setup to read the existing SMS or voice authentication method configuration. | +| Update authentication method policy | Authentication Policy Administrator and delegated `Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod` permission | Allows setup to configure the SMS or voice authentication method to use the integration. | + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Before you begin, confirm that your Microsoft Entra policies allow the setup script to create the application and credentials it needs. If you use app management policies for credentials, multitenant apps, or custom Application ID URIs, review them with your Microsoft Entra administrator. + +## Step 1: Purchase and activate your telecom provider + +1. Purchase your provider's offer from [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/). For detailed purchasing instructions, see [Purchase and deploy a SaaS solution from Security Store](/security/store/customers/how-to-purchase-a-saas-solution-and-deploy-a-linked-solution). +1. After you **Place Order**, select **Configure Account Now** and follow your provider's registration instructions. +1. Keep this page available and continue to step 2. You'll complete registration in step 3 with the application ID from the deployment summary. + +## Step 2: Deploy the integration + +Use Azure Cloud Shell in PowerShell mode to run the setup script for the telecom provider you select. + +### What the setup script does + +The setup script deploys everything needed to connect Microsoft Entra ID to your telecom provider, so you don't have to create Azure resources by hand. It walks you through a few choices, then shows the full deployment plan. Nothing is created until you approve it. + +After you approve, the script creates the Microsoft Entra application, deploys and secures the Azure resources, and applies your provider's configuration. Deployment usually takes a few minutes. + +You configure the authentication method policy in step 4. + +Your organization is responsible for renewing and rotating the integration's application credentials and certificates. + +### Costs + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The integration runs on Azure resources in your subscription, billed based on your configuration and usage. To plan your budget, see [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost) before you deploy. + +### Run the setup script + +1. Sign in to the Azure portal and select the **Cloud Shell** icon (**>_**) in the top toolbar. You can also go directly to . +1. Select **PowerShell**. If Cloud Shell opens in Bash, select **Switch to PowerShell** in the toolbar. +1. If this is your first time, select **No storage account required**, choose your subscription, and then select **Apply**. +1. Download and review the [setup script](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/setup/Setup-Epp.ps1): + + ```powershell + Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/main/setup/Setup-Epp.ps1' ` + -OutFile '.\Setup-Epp.ps1' + ``` + +1. Run the script. + + ```powershell + .\Setup-Epp.ps1 + ``` + +1. Follow the prompts to select the customer tenant, hosting subscription, Azure region, telecom provider, runtime, and hosting plan, then approve the deployment plan. +1. Save the deployment summary, including its tenant ID, endpoint URL, and **Application (client) ID**. You need these values to complete provider registration and configure your profile. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Copy these values before you leave the Cloud Shell window. Cloud Shell sessions are temporary and can end when you navigate away, and the output isn't saved. + +## Step 3: Complete telecom provider registration + +After deployment completes, return to your telecom provider's registration page to complete the provider setup. + +1. Provide the **Application (client) ID** from your Microsoft Entra application when requested by your telecom provider. +1. Complete any additional registration steps required by the provider. +1. In [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/), go to **Management** > **My Solutions** and confirm that the **Subscription status** is '**Subscribed**' before continuing. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Complete the telecom provider registration before configuring Microsoft Entra to send authentication traffic through the provider. + +## Step 4: Update the authentication method policy + +Configure each channel with the endpoint URL and application client ID from the deployment summary. Start in evaluation mode, validate the integration, and then gradually move delivery to your telecom provider. + +> [!WARNING] +> CYOT uses the existing SMS or voice authentication method policy. Changes to the policy, including changes to `includeTargets`, also affect the existing SMS or voice configuration. +> +> Before making updates, save the current SMS and voice settings by copying the full JSON responses from [Read the current policy](#read-the-current-policy). +> +> In a production tenant, preserve the existing `includeTargets` configuration when adding CYOT settings. Changing or removing existing targets can affect users who rely on SMS or voice authentication. +> +> Test targeting changes in a test tenant. In production, preserve the existing SMS or voice `includeTargets` and use evaluation mode plus `migrationPercentage` to validate and gradually roll out CYOT. + +### Read the current policy + +Use [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to read and update the policy. Confirm that you're signed in to the tenant whose ID matches the Tenant ID in the deployment summary. + +Use these request URLs for the corresponding channel: + +| Channel | Request URL | +|---|---| +| SMS | `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/Sms` | +| Voice | `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/Voice` | + +1. Set the request method to **GET** and enter the corresponding channel's request URL. +1. Open **Modify permissions** and consent to `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod`. +1. Select **Run query** and save the complete JSON response as a record of the existing policy. +1. Repeat for the other channel if you're configuring both SMS and voice. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> When you prepare the updated policy, use the saved response to preserve your existing `includeTargets` and other intended authentication method settings. + +### Configure CYOT settings + +Configure these properties: + +| Property | Value | +|---|---| +| `telecomProviderSettings.url` | Endpoint URL from the deployment summary. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.appId` | Integration application client ID. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.isEvaluationModeEnabled` | Set to `true` for evaluation mode or `false` to enable telecom provider delivery. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.migrationPercentage` | Percentage of eligible authentication requests sampled during evaluation, or routed to your telecom provider when evaluation mode is disabled. | +| `includeTargets` | Preserve the existing production configuration. These targets are shared with the existing SMS or voice authentication method policy. | + +### Start in evaluation mode + +Start in evaluation mode to validate the integration before moving authentication delivery to your telecom provider. + +Use `migrationPercentage` to set the evaluation sampling percentage. + +1. Use the tested SMS or voice JSON example provided below in **Request body**. +1. Replace the endpoint URL and application client ID with the values for your deployment. +1. Set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `true`. +1. For production tenants, preserve the existing `includeTargets` from your saved policy configuration. Do not replace existing production targeting for CYOT testing. +1. Open **Modify permissions**, consent to `Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod`, and send the **PATCH** request to the corresponding channel's URL. +1. Read the policy again with **GET** and verify the endpoint URL, application client ID, evaluation-mode setting, migration percentage, and existing targets. +1. Complete the [evaluation-mode tests](#test-evaluation-mode) in step 5. + +> [!NOTE] +> To evaluate CYOT with a specific test user or group, perform the test in a test tenant and configure the appropriate `includeTargets` there. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The JSON examples below contain the tested configuration values. Before using an example, replace the endpoint URL and application client ID with the values for your deployment. +> +> For evaluation mode, set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `true`. In a production tenant, preserve the `includeTargets` from your existing SMS or voice policy rather than replacing them with the values shown in the example. Use a test tenant if you want to validate CYOT with different target users or groups. + +For SMS: + +```json +{ + "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.smsAuthenticationMethodConfiguration", + "state": "enabled", + "includeTargets": [ + { + "targetType": "group", + "id": "all_users", + "isRegistrationRequired": false, + "isUsableForSignIn": false + } + ], + "telecomProviderSettings": { + "url": "", + "appId": "", + "isEvaluationModeEnabled": false, + "migrationPercentage": 100 + } +} +``` + +For Voice: + +```json +{ + "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.voiceAuthenticationMethodConfiguration", + "state": "enabled", + "includeTargets": [ + { + "targetType": "group", + "id": "all_users", + "isRegistrationRequired": false, + "verificationMode": "voiceOneTimePasscode" + } + ], + "telecomProviderSettings": { + "url": "", + "appId": "", + "isEvaluationModeEnabled": false, + "migrationPercentage": 100 + } +} +``` + +### Move to production mode + +After evaluation succeeds: + +1. Set `telecomProviderSettings.isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `false`. +1. Set `telecomProviderSettings.migrationPercentage` to your initial traffic percentage. +1. Keep the existing production `includeTargets` unchanged. +1. Submit the policy update. +1. Read the configuration again and verify the endpoint URL, application client ID, evaluation mode, migration percentage, and targets. +1. Test [telecom provider delivery](#test-telecom-provider-delivery) before increasing traffic. + +### Increase traffic gradually + +1. Keep `isEvaluationModeEnabled` set to `false`. +1. Increase `migrationPercentage` in increments until you reach `100`. +1. Keep the endpoint URL, application client ID, and existing `includeTargets` unchanged while changing the migration percentage. +1. [Validate authentication and telecom provider delivery](#check-each-rollout-stage) after each change. +1. Increase the percentage after each stage validates successfully. To investigate an issue, hold at the current percentage and see [Monitor and troubleshoot](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> When each stage validates successfully, continue to 100 percent without delay. Completing your rollout early helps ensure uninterrupted authentication for your users. For dates, see [Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication](concept-sms-voice-retirement.md). + +## Step 5: Test the integration + +Use a test user with a phone number registered for SMS or voice. + + + +### Test in Evaluation + +1. In an InPrivate browser session, sign in as the test user and complete an SMS or voice authentication. +1. In the Azure portal, go to your **Function App** > **SendOtp** > **Invocations** and open the latest transaction. In **Invocation details**, confirm **Evaluation request completed** with HTTP `200`. +1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Monitoring & health** > **Audit logs** and filter by **Service: Azure MFA**. Open the latest entry and confirm **DeliveryMethod** is `CyotEvaluation`. + + + + +### Test provider delivery + +After evaluation succeeds, set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `false` and configure your initial `migrationPercentage`. + +1. In a new InPrivate browser session, sign in as the test user. Confirm the SMS or voice code arrives and authentication completes. +1. In the Azure portal, go to your **Function App** > **Invocations** and open the latest transaction. In **Invocation details**, confirm the request completed with HTTP `200`. +1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Audit logs** and filter by **Service: Azure MFA**. Open the latest entry and confirm **Delivery Method** is `Cyot`. +1. In your provider's portal, confirm the message was delivered. + +At a partial percentage, only some requests route through your provider, so make a few attempts. If something doesn't look right, see [Monitor and troubleshoot your own telephony provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +## Troubleshooting + +To diagnose integration issues, use the troubleshooting guide to identify whether the issue is with the Microsoft Entra configuration, Azure Function, telecom provider, or authentication flow. + +See [Monitor and troubleshoot your own telephony provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider) for diagnostic steps, logs, common issues, and remediation guidance. + +## Related content + +- [Monitor and troubleshoot](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Plan for resiliency when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-troubleshoot.md b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-troubleshoot.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..26d82eac1eb --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-troubleshoot.md @@ -0,0 +1,164 @@ +--- +title: Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider +description: Trace CYOT SMS and voice requests with audit logs, sign-in logs, and Function App logs to identify issues and contact the right support team. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1012 +ms.reviewer: xueca +# Customer intent: As an authentication administrator, I want to identify and resolve CYOT authentication, integration, and telecom delivery issues. +--- + +# Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider + + + + + +Use this article to trace SMS and voice requests end to end with Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), find where a request stopped, and contact the right team to resolve it: Microsoft support, your Azure team, or your telecom provider. + + + + + + +## How a CYOT request flows + +Each request passes through four stages, and each stage is recorded in its own logs: + +| Stage | What happens | Where to look | +|---|---|---| +| 1. Microsoft Entra sends the request | Microsoft Entra requires an SMS or voice code and sends the request to your endpoint. | Microsoft Entra audit logs | +| 2. Your endpoint processes it | Your Function App receives the request and sends it to your telecom provider. | Function App logs | +| 3. Your provider delivers it | Your provider sends the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | Your provider's portal | +| 4. The user signs in | The user enters the code, and Microsoft Entra completes authentication. | Microsoft Entra sign-in logs | + +## Find the request in audit logs + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a Reports Reader. +1. +# Include access packages in catalog access reviews (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra ID Governance now supports including access packages in catalog access reviews (preview). When a user has access to Microsoft Entra applications or Microsoft Entra groups through an access package, reviewers see the access package instead of separate entries for each resource it contains.
+
+This article explains how to enable access packages in a catalog access review, who reviews them, and what happens when a reviewer denies an access package.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite subscription. For more information, see [Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing fundamentals](licensing-fundamentals.md).
+- At least the [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator) role to create the catalog access review.
+- A catalog that contains the access packages you want to review.
+
+## Include access packages in a review
+
+Enable the access package preview option when you create the catalog access review.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Access reviews** > **New access review**.
+1. Select **Review users access across multiple resource types within a catalog**.
+1. Enter the basic information for the review, and then select **Next**.
+1. On the **Resources** tab, use **Select Catalog** to select the catalog that contains the access packages you want to review.
+1. Select **Include access packages (Preview)**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/catalog-access-reviews/include-access-packages.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Resources tab with the Include access packages (Preview) checkbox selected beneath Select Catalog.":::
+
+1. Select **Next**. On the **Reviewers and schedule** tab, choose the reviewers and configure the schedule.
+
+    If you choose resource owners as reviewers, the access package assignment manager for each specific access package reviews that package.
+
+1. Configure the reviewer experience and completion settings, and then select **Create**.
+
+For more information about the review settings, see [Create a catalog access review](catalog-access-reviews.md#create-a-catalog-access-review).
+
+## Review access package assignments
+
+Reviewers review an access package as a single item, rather than deciding separately on each Microsoft Entra group or application granted through that package.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Only Microsoft Entra applications and Microsoft Entra groups delivered through access packages are consolidated under the access package in the review.
+
+1. Sign in to the [My Access portal](https://myaccess.microsoft.com) as a reviewer.
+1. Select **Access reviews**, and then select the **Multi-resource** tab.
+1. Open the catalog access review.
+1. For each access package, select **Approve** or **Deny**, and provide a justification if required.
+1. Select **Submit** to record your decisions.
+
+When a reviewer denies an access package, the user's access package assignment is removed on the review end date. Removing the assignment removes the user's access to all resources granted through that package, not just the Microsoft Entra applications and Microsoft Entra groups consolidated in the review.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Create a catalog access review](catalog-access-reviews.md).
+- [Delegate access package management](entitlement-management-delegate-managers.md).
+- [Create an access review of an access package in entitlement management](entitlement-management-access-reviews-create.md).

+---
+title: Microsoft Entra External ID credential management API reference
+description: Use the Microsoft Entra External ID credential management API to let signed-in customers list, register, and delete their passkeys.
+author: mmacy-msft
+manager: dougeby
+ms.author: marshmacy
+ms.service: identity-platform
+ms.subservice: external
+ms.topic: reference
+ms.date: 10/29/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+#Customer intent: As an identity developer, I want to learn how to integrate the credential management API into my customer-facing app so that customers can list, register, and delete their own credential methods.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra External ID credential management API reference
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+The Microsoft Entra External ID credential management API lets your application give signed-in customers a self-service flow for listing, registering, and deleting passkeys. Your application owns the client experience and calls the API on the customer's behalf.
+
+The credential management API complements Microsoft Entra [native authentication](concept-native-authentication.md), where your application hosts the sign-in experience instead of delegating it to a browser. Use the credential management API after a customer signs in.
+
+To support passkey management in your app, use the [passkey credential management sample app](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-ciam-native-javascript-samples/tree/main/passkey-sample). The sample demonstrates the listing and registration flows in this article by using delegated permissions. Follow the sample's README to configure and run the app.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> The sample's deletion flow still uses Microsoft Graph with high-privilege application permissions and a client secret in browser code. Run the sample only in a test tenant. Don't deploy it to production.
+
+For self-service deletion, use the [Delete a credential method](#delete-a-credential-method) endpoint rather than the sample's deletion flow.
+
+Successful resource responses use HAL+JSON (`application/hal+json`). Activation requests use JSON (`application/json`), delete success responses have no body, and errors use JSON.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Microsoft Entra external tenant. If you don't already have one, [create an external tenant](../external-id/customers/how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md).
+
+- An application [registered in the Microsoft Entra admin center](quickstart-register-app.md). Record the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** for later use.
+
+## Configure credential management API access
+
+Before your app can acquire access tokens for the credential management API, provision the API's service principal and add a delegated permission:
+
+1. Provision the credential management API's service principal in your tenant. The credential management API is a Microsoft-published resource. Until automatic provisioning is available, you must create its service principal manually. In [Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), sign in as an administrator of the tenant where you want to provision it, then run:
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "appId": "6bf38b3c-a70f-49aa-a1d9-10e4cc74dde9"
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Add a delegated permission to your app for the credential management API. For passkeys, the least-privileged choice is `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.Read` (read) or `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite` (write). See [Authentication and authorization](#authentication-and-authorization) for the full list of accepted permissions. Grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.
+
+## Authentication and authorization
+
+The credential management API acts on behalf of a signed-in customer. Every endpoint URL has the form `https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/...`, where `{tenant-subdomain}` is your external tenant's subdomain, `{tenant-id}` is your external tenant's ID, and `me` is the customer whose access token you send with the request. Your application:
+
+1. Signs the customer in.
+1. Obtains an access token for the credential management API.
+1. Includes that token on every call.
+
+Without a signed-in customer, `me` has no meaning and the call can't be authenticated. If you've worked with Microsoft Graph or other Microsoft Entra REST APIs, this follows the same model: standard OAuth 2.0 with delegated permissions.
+
+Include the access token in the standard HTTP `Authorization` header on every request:
+
+```http
+Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
+```
+
+### Acquire a delegated access token
+
+Use a delegated access token to call the credential management API on behalf of the signed-in customer. The API rejects app-only tokens, including tokens acquired through the client credentials flow. When the customer signs in, request one of the permissions listed in [Required permissions](#required-permissions). The requested permission determines the token audience; you don't set the audience separately.
+
+The following diagram shows how a call is authenticated, from signing the customer in to calling the API with the resulting token.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/reference-credential-management-api/authentication-authorization-flow.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram that shows your app signing the customer in to get an access token for the credential management API, then calling the API with that token while Microsoft Entra External ID validates it." lightbox="media/reference-credential-management-api/authentication-authorization-flow.png":::
+
+Acquire the delegated token through the Microsoft Entra sign-in flow that applies to your application:
+
+- Single-page, mobile, and desktop apps: use the [Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL)](msal-overview.md).
+- Server-side web apps: use the [OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow](v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow.md) with PKCE.
+- Apps using native authentication: use the [native authentication API](reference-native-authentication-api.md) to sign in or sign up the customer, then redeem the result for an access token at the `/token` endpoint.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> For native authentication, only the web experience is supported for now. Native authentication on mobile platforms (Android and iOS) isn't currently supported for the credential management API.
+
+Pass the resulting token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every credential management API call.
+
+### Required permissions
+
+All permissions are delegated permissions exposed by the credential management API. Add one to your app registration and request it when you sign the customer in. Because this release supports passkeys only, the passkey-scoped permissions are the least-privileged choice.
+
+| Operation | Accepted delegated permissions (least privileged first) |
+| --- | --- |
+| Read (for example, listing the customer's passkeys) | `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.Read`, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Read`, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite`, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite` |
+| Write (for example, registering or deleting a passkey) | `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite`, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite` |
+
+Application-only access (the client credentials flow) isn't supported.
+
+## Continuation token
+
+When you call a multi-step operation such as registering a passkey, the credential management API returns a continuation token in the response. This token uniquely identifies the current flow and lets Microsoft Entra maintain state across its endpoints. Include the token in every subsequent request in that flow. It's valid only for a limited time and can only be used for the subsequent requests within the same flow.
+
+## Supported credential methods
+
+In this release, the credential management API supports one type of credential method:
+
+| Method | URL segment (`{type}`) | Description |
+|--------|------------------------|-------------|
+| Passkey | `fido` | A phishing-resistant credential based on the WebAuthn standard. |
+
+Other credential methods, such as software OATH one-time passcodes, email, phone, and recovery methods, aren't supported by this API yet.
+
+## List user credential methods
+
+Returns the credential methods the signed-in customer has currently registered, along with the method types they can still register. For example, your app calls this endpoint when rendering a page where the customer can review their existing passkeys and start registering a new one.
+
+The following sequence diagram shows the list flow.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/reference-credential-management-api/list-credential-methods.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram that shows your app calling the list endpoint with the customer's access token and Microsoft Entra External ID returning the registered and available-to-register methods in HAL+JSON." lightbox="media/reference-credential-management-api/list-credential-methods.png":::
+
+See [Authentication and authorization](#authentication-and-authorization) for the access token your application needs to call this endpoint. This endpoint accepts any of the read or write permissions listed in [Required permissions](#required-permissions).
+
+### HTTP request
+
+```http
+GET https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods
+```
+
+`{tenant-subdomain}` in the URL is your external tenant's subdomain, for example *contoso* in *contoso.ciamlogin.com*.
+
+Sample request:
+
+```http
+GET https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/8f1c8e2a-1234-4abc-9876-1f1e1d1c1b1a/api/v1.0/me/methods HTTP/1.1
+Host: contoso.ciamlogin.com
+Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
+```
+
+### Request parameters
+
+Path parameters:
+
+| Name | Required | Description |
+|------|----------|-------------|
+| `tenant-id` | Yes | Your external tenant identifier, either the tenant ID (GUID) or a verified domain. Use a tenant-specific value, not `common`, `client`, `organizations`, or `consumers`. A GUID value must match the tenant in the access token. |
+
+Request headers:
+
+| Name | Required | Value |
+|------|----------|-------|
+| `Authorization` | Yes | `Bearer <access_token>` |
+
+This endpoint doesn't perform `Accept`-header content negotiation. The response is always `application/hal+json` regardless of the `Accept` header value.
+
+### Success response
+
+Here's an example of a successful response:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Type: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "_embedded": {
+    "methods": [
+      {
+        "aaGuid": "<authenticator-aaguid>",
+        "attestationLevel": "notAttested",
+        "model": "Windows Hello VBS Hardware Authenticator",
+        "passkeyType": "deviceBound",
+        "displayName": "<display-name>",
+        "id": "<credential-id-1>",
+        "type": "fido",
+        "createdDateTime": "<timestamp>",
+        "_links": {
+          "self": {
+            "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-1}",
+            "name": "self"
+          },
+          "delete": {
+            "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-1}",
+            "name": "delete"
+          }
+        }
+      },
+      {
+        "aaGuid": "<authenticator-aaguid>",
+        "attestationCertificates": [
+          "<certificate-thumbprint>"
+        ],
+        "attestationLevel": "attested",
+        "model": "YubiKey 5 FIPS Series with NFC",
+        "passkeyType": "deviceBound",
+        "displayName": "<display-name>",
+        "id": "<credential-id-2>",
+        "type": "fido",
+        "createdDateTime": "<timestamp>",
+        "_links": {
+          "self": {
+            "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-2}",
+            "name": "self"
+          },
+          "delete": {
+            "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-2}",
+            "name": "delete"
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    ]
+  },
+  "_links": {
+    "self": {
+      "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods",
+      "name": "self"
+    },
+    "enroll": [
+      {
+        "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido",
+        "name": "fido"
+      }
+    ],
+    "methods": [
+      {
+        "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-1}",
+        "name": "<credential-id-1>"
+      },
+      {
+        "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id-2}",
+        "name": "<credential-id-2>"
+      }
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Follow the returned HAL links instead of constructing operation URLs from identifiers.
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `_embedded.methods` | array of objects | Yes | Registered credential methods. The array is present even when the customer has no registered methods. |
+| `_links.self` | object | Yes | Link to the credential-method collection. |
+| `_links.enroll` | array of objects | No | Enrollment links, one for each credential type the customer can register. |
+| `_links.methods` | array of objects | No | Links to the customer's registered methods. |
+
+#### Registered passkey properties
+
+Authenticator-specific properties can vary or be absent. For example, a nonattested passkey can omit `attestationCertificates`, while an attested device-bound passkey can include certificate values.
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `id` | string | Yes | Durable, case-sensitive base64url identifier for the registered passkey. |
+| `type` | string | Yes | Credential method type. The value is `fido`. |
+| `createdDateTime` | string | No | Time when the passkey was registered. |
+| `lastUsedDateTime` | string | No | Time when the passkey was last used. |
+| `aaGuid` | string | No | Authenticator Attestation GUID (AAGUID), when returned by the authenticator. |
+| `attestationCertificates` | array of strings | No | Attestation certificate values, when the authenticator provides attestation. |
+| `attestationLevel` | string | No | Attestation level reported for the authenticator. |
+| `model` | string | No | Authenticator model. |
+| `passkeyType` | string | No | Passkey classification reported by the service. |
+| `displayName` | string | No | Customer-provided passkey name. |
+| `_links` | object | Yes | `self` and `delete` links for the registered passkey. |
+
+This endpoint can return `400`, `401`, or `403`. For the shared envelope and caller actions, see [Error responses](#error-responses).
+
+## Provisioning
+
+Provisioning a passkey for the signed-in customer takes two HTTP calls. First, your application calls the begin registration endpoint, which returns WebAuthn creation options, a continuation token, and an `activate` link. The customer's authenticator uses the creation options to create a new passkey. Your application then calls the activate endpoint with the result to complete registration. Start this flow when the customer chooses to add a passkey in your application's credential-management experience.
+
+The following sequence diagram shows the two-step provisioning flow.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/reference-credential-management-api/provision-passkey.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram that shows begin registration returning a WebAuthn challenge and continuation token, the authenticator creating the passkey, and the activate call registering the passkey with Microsoft Entra External ID." lightbox="media/reference-credential-management-api/provision-passkey.png":::
+
+See [Authentication and authorization](#authentication-and-authorization) for the access token your application needs to call these endpoints. Both calls require a write permission, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite` or `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite` (see [Required permissions](#required-permissions)).
+
+### Step 1: Begin registration
+
+#### HTTP request
+
+```http
+POST https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/{type}
+```
+
+`{tenant-subdomain}` in the URL is your external tenant's subdomain, for example *contoso* in *contoso.ciamlogin.com*.
+
+Sample request:
+
+```http
+POST https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/8f1c8e2a-1234-4abc-9876-1f1e1d1c1b1a/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido HTTP/1.1
+Host: contoso.ciamlogin.com
+Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
+```
+
+#### Request parameters
+
+Path parameters:
+
+| Name | Required | Description |
+|------|----------|-------------|
+| `tenant-id` | Yes | Your external tenant identifier, either the tenant ID (GUID) or a verified domain. Use a tenant-specific value, not `common`, `client`, `organizations`, or `consumers`. A GUID value must match the tenant in the access token. |
+| `type` | Yes | The credential method type to register. Currently only `fido` (passkey) is supported. |
+
+Request headers:
+
+| Name | Required | Value |
+|------|----------|-------|
+| `Authorization` | Yes | `Bearer <access_token>` |
+
+This endpoint doesn't take a request body. All inputs are carried in the URL path and the `Authorization` header.
+
+#### Success response
+
+Here's an example of a successful response:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
+Content-Type: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "publicKey": {
+    "rp": {
+      "id": "<relying-party-id>",
+      "name": "Microsoft"
+    },
+    "user": {
+      "id": "<user-handle>",
+      "name": "<user-name>",
+      "displayName": "<user-display-name>"
+    },
+    "challenge": "<challenge>",
+    "pubKeyCredParams": [
+      {
+        "type": "public-key",
+        "alg": -7
+      },
+      {
+        "type": "public-key",
+        "alg": -257
+      }
+    ],
+    "timeout": 0,
+    "excludeCredentials": [
+      {
+        "type": "public-key",
+        "id": "<excluded-credential-id>",
+        "transports": []
+      }
+    ],
+    "authenticatorSelection": {
+      "authenticatorAttachment": "cross-platform",
+      "requireResidentKey": true,
+      "userVerification": "required"
+    },
+    "attestation": "direct",
+    "extensions": {
+      "hmacCreateSecret": true,
+      "enforceCredentialProtectionPolicy": true,
+      "credentialProtectionPolicy": "userVerificationOptional"
+    }
+  },
+  "challengeTimeout": "<timestamp>",
+  "id": "<registration-id>",
+  "type": "fido",
+  "continuationToken": "<continuation-token>",
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "activate",
+  "_links": {
+    "self": {
+      "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{registration-id}",
+      "name": "self"
+    },
+    "activate": {
+      "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{registration-id}/activate",
+      "name": "activate"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The response has the following properties:
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `id` | string | Yes | Transient identifier for the in-progress registration. |
+| `type` | string | Yes | Credential method type. The value is `fido`. |
+| `publicKey` | object | No | WebAuthn credential creation options for the client ceremony. |
+| `challengeTimeout` | string | No | Time when the challenge expires. |
+| `state` | string | Yes | Flow state. The value is `interactionRequired`. |
+| `action` | string | Yes | Next action. The value is `activate`. |
+| `continuationToken` | string | Yes | Opaque state that must be returned during activation. |
+| `_links` | object | Yes | `self` and `activate` links for the in-progress registration. |
+
+The `publicKey` object aligns with the common fields in [webauthnPublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions](/graph/api/resources/webauthnpublickeycredentialcreationoptions). The service can also preserve additional WebAuthn properties for forward compatibility.
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `rp` | object | No | Relying-party information. |
+| `user` | object | No | User information for the registration ceremony. |
+| `challenge` | string | No | Base64url-encoded WebAuthn challenge. |
+| `pubKeyCredParams` | array of objects | No | Supported public-key credential types and algorithms. |
+| `timeout` | integer | No | Ceremony timeout in milliseconds. |
+| `excludeCredentials` | array of objects | No | Existing credentials that the authenticator should exclude. |
+| `authenticatorSelection` | object | No | Authenticator selection requirements. |
+| `attestation` | string | No | Requested attestation conveyance preference. |
+| `hints` | array of strings | No | Optional authenticator hints. |
+| `extensions` | object | No | WebAuthn extension inputs. |
+
+Pass `publicKey` to the customer's authenticator to create the passkey. Preserve `continuationToken` exactly, and follow `_links.activate.href` for the activation request.
+
+The begin registration endpoint can return `400`, `401`, `403`, or `500`. For the shared envelope and caller actions, see [Error responses](#error-responses).
+
+### Step 2: Activate the passkey
+
+#### HTTP request
+
+```http
+POST https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/{type}/{id}/activate
+```
+
+`{tenant-subdomain}` in the URL is your external tenant's subdomain, for example *contoso* in *contoso.ciamlogin.com*.
+
+Sample request:
+
+```http
+POST https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/8f1c8e2a-1234-4abc-9876-1f1e1d1c1b1a/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{registration-id}/activate HTTP/1.1
+Host: contoso.ciamlogin.com
+Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
+Content-Type: application/json
+
+{
+  "continuationToken": "<continuation-token>",
+  "displayName": "My laptop",
+  "publicKeyCredential": {
+    "id": "<credential-id>",
+    "attestationObject": "<attestation-object>",
+    "clientDataJSON": "<client-data-json>"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+#### Request parameters
+
+Path parameters:
+
+| Name | Required | Description |
+|------|----------|-------------|
+| `tenant-id` | Yes | Your external tenant identifier, either the tenant ID (GUID) or a verified domain. Use a tenant-specific value, not `common`, `client`, `organizations`, or `consumers`. A GUID value must match the tenant in the access token. |
+| `type` | Yes | The credential method type being registered. Currently only `fido` (passkey) is supported. Must match the value used in the begin registration step. |
+| `id` | Yes | The in-progress registration identifier returned by the begin registration step. Take it from `_links.activate.href` in the begin registration response rather than constructing it yourself. |
+
+Request headers:
+
+| Name | Required | Value |
+|------|----------|-------|
+| `Authorization` | Yes | `Bearer <access_token>` |
+| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` |
+
+#### Request body
+
+A JSON object with the following fields:
+
+| Name | Type | Required | Description |
+|------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `continuationToken` | string | Yes | The opaque token returned by the begin registration response. It carries the server-side state of the in-progress registration so Microsoft Entra can resume exactly where it left off. Treat it as opaque and don't parse or modify it. See [Continuation token](#continuation-token). |
+| `displayName` | string | No | A friendly name the customer gives the passkey, for example *My laptop*. |
+| `publicKeyCredential` | object | No | WebAuthn credential data produced by the customer's authenticator. |
+
+The `publicKeyCredential` value is derived from the WebAuthn [PublicKeyCredential](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/#iface-publickeycredential). The API flattens the credential ID, attestation response, and extension results into the following properties:
+
+| Name | Type | Required | Description |
+|------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `id` | string | No | Base64url-encoded credential identifier returned by the authenticator. |
+| `attestationObject` | string | No | Base64url-encoded attestation object returned by the authenticator. |
+| `clientDataJSON` | string | No | Base64url-encoded client data returned by the authenticator. |
+| `clientExtensionResults` | string | No | Serialized WebAuthn client extension results. |
+
+#### Success response
+
+Here's an example of a successful response:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 201 Created
+Content-Type: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "aaGuid": "<authenticator-aaguid>",
+  "attestationLevel": "notAttested",
+  "model": "Windows Hello VBS Hardware Authenticator",
+  "passkeyType": "deviceBound",
+  "displayName": "<display-name>",
+  "id": "<credential-id>",
+  "type": "fido",
+  "createdDateTime": "<timestamp>",
+  "_links": {
+    "self": {
+      "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id}",
+      "name": "self"
+    },
+    "delete": {
+      "href": "/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{credential-id}",
+      "name": "delete"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The activation response has the following properties:
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `id` | string | Yes | Identifier returned for the registered passkey. |
+| `type` | string | Yes | Credential method type. The value is `fido`. |
+| `createdDateTime` | string | No | Time when registration completed. |
+| `aaGuid` | string | No | Authenticator Attestation GUID (AAGUID), when returned by the authenticator. |
+| `attestationCertificates` | array of strings | No | Attestation certificate values, when the authenticator provides attestation. |
+| `attestationLevel` | string | No | Attestation level reported for the authenticator. |
+| `model` | string | No | Authenticator model. |
+| `passkeyType` | string | No | Passkey classification reported by the service. |
+| `_links` | object | Yes | `self` and `delete` links for the registered passkey. |
+
+Authenticator-specific properties can vary or be absent. The activation endpoint can return `400`, `401`, or `403`. For the shared envelope and caller actions, see [Error responses](#error-responses).
+
+## Delete a credential method
+
+Permanently deletes one of the signed-in customer's registered passkeys. Use this endpoint after [listing the customer's credential methods](#list-user-credential-methods) and when the customer chooses to remove a passkey in your application's credential-management flow. Deletion is immediate and can't be undone. A replacement passkey is a new credential with no relation to the deleted passkey.
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> If the customer deletes the passkey they used to sign in to their current session, that session ends.
+
+The following sequence diagram shows the delete flow.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/reference-credential-management-api/delete-credential-method.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram that shows your app calling the delete endpoint with the customer's access token and Microsoft Entra External ID removing the passkey and returning 204 No Content." lightbox="media/reference-credential-management-api/delete-credential-method.png":::
+
+See [Authentication and authorization](#authentication-and-authorization) for the access token your application needs to call this endpoint. This endpoint requires a write permission, `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite` or `Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite` (see [Required permissions](#required-permissions)).
+
+### HTTP request
+
+```http
+DELETE https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/methods/{type}/{id}
+```
+
+`{tenant-subdomain}` in the URL is your external tenant's subdomain, for example *contoso* in *contoso.ciamlogin.com*.
+
+Sample request:
+
+```http
+DELETE https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/8f1c8e2a-1234-4abc-9876-1f1e1d1c1b1a/api/v1.0/me/methods/fido/{id} HTTP/1.1
+Host: contoso.ciamlogin.com
+Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
+```
+
+### Request parameters
+
+Path parameters:
+
+| Name | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `tenant-id` | Yes | Your external tenant identifier, either the tenant ID (GUID) or a verified domain. Use a tenant-specific value, not `common`, `client`, `organizations`, or `consumers`. A GUID value must match the tenant in the access token. |
+| `type` | Yes | The credential method type to delete. Currently only `fido` (passkey) is supported. |
+| `id` | Yes | The identifier of the registered passkey to delete. Use the `id` (or follow the `delete` link) from [List user credential methods](#list-user-credential-methods), the source of truth for the customer's registered methods. |
+
+Request headers:
+
+| Name | Required | Value |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `Authorization` | Yes | `Bearer <access_token>` |
+
+This endpoint doesn't take a request body. The passkey to delete is identified entirely by the URL.
+
+### Success response
+
+A successful delete returns an empty response:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
+```
+
+This endpoint can return `400`, `401`, or `403`. For the shared envelope and caller actions, see [Error responses](#error-responses).
+
+## Error responses
+
+Error responses use a shared JSON envelope. The following example shows the required properties:
+
+```json
+{
+  "error": {
+    "code": "invalidRequest",
+    "message": "<error-message>",
+    "timestamp": "<timestamp>",
+    "traceId": "<trace-id>",
+    "correlationId": "<correlation-id>"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The error response has the following properties:
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+|----------|------|----------|-------------|
+| `error` | object | Yes | Error details. |
+| `error.code` | string | Yes | Machine-readable error code. |
+| `error.message` | string | Yes | Human-readable description of the failure. Don't use this value for programmatic branching. |
+| `error.timestamp` | string | Yes | Time when the error occurred. |
+| `error.traceId` | string | Yes | Identifier used to trace the request. |
+| `error.correlationId` | string | Yes | Identifier used to correlate the request across components. |
+| `error.target` | string | No | Request element associated with the error. |
+| `error.innerError` | object | No | Additional error details. |
+| `clientHints` | array of strings | No | Optional response-wide hint tokens. |
+
+The following status and code combinations are confirmed for these endpoints:
+
+| HTTP status | Error code | Confirmed causes |
+|-------------|------------|------------------|
+| `400 Bad Request` | `invalidRequest` | Missing or malformed bearer token, invalid token signature, expired token, app-only token, insufficient delegated scope, a non-specific tenant route, or invalid registration state such as a malformed continuation token. |
+| `401 Unauthorized` | `invalidRequest` | The token wasn't issued for the credential management API. |
+| `403 Forbidden` | `forbidden` | The tenant in the request URL doesn't match the tenant in the access token. |
+| `500 Internal Server Error` | `serverError` | The begin registration endpoint received an invalid WebAuthn creation-options response from an upstream component. |
+
+The shared error model also defines `unknown`, `invalidGrant`, `expiredToken`, `tooManyRequests`, and `unsupportedRedirect`. Don't assume that every endpoint emits every code.
+
+Handle confirmed errors as follows:
+
+| Response | Caller action |
+|----------|---------------|
+| `400 invalidRequest` | Use `error.message` to diagnose the invalid input. Acquire a new delegated token when the token is missing, malformed, invalid, expired, app-only, or lacks an accepted scope. Use a tenant-specific route value. If registration state is invalid, restart the two-step registration flow. |
+| `401 invalidRequest` | Request an accepted credential management API permission when acquiring the token, then retry the request. |
+| `403 forbidden` | Verify that the `{tenant-id}` in the request URL matches the tenant represented by the access token. |
+| `500 serverError` | Record `traceId` and `correlationId` for diagnostics. Don't assume that the operation succeeded. |

While telecom-based MFA provides an important layer of security, methods like passkeys, certificate-based authentication, and Windows Hello for Business offer stronger protection against interception and social engineering attacks. -> -> These methods also avoid the delivery variability inherent in global telecom networks. These providers rely on their own networks of suppliers, who control the routes for SMS and voice calls through local end-carrier networks. This supply chain represents thousands of individual carriers and routes around the globe. +## How a CYOT request flows -Microsoft maintains robust processes to help ensure successful delivery of every SMS and voice MFA request. However, once a request leaves the Microsoft network, delivery is delegated to external telecom providers. +Each request passes through four stages, and each stage is recorded in its own logs: -These providers often share the same end routes and carriers in a given destination country but might operate under different contractual agreements or traffic priorities. As a result, routing a request through a different provider doesn't always resolve the issue — the new request might follow the same downstream path and encounter the same obstacle. +| Stage | What happens | Where to look | +|---|---|---| +| 1. Microsoft Entra sends the request | Microsoft Entra requires an SMS or voice code and sends the request to your endpoint. | Microsoft Entra audit logs | +| 2. Your endpoint processes it | Your Function App receives the request and sends it to your telecom provider. | Function App logs | +| 3. Your provider delivers it | Your provider sends the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | Your provider's portal | +| 4. The user signs in | The user enters the code, and Microsoft Entra completes authentication. | Microsoft Entra sign-in logs | -## The journey of an SMS or voice MFA request +## Find the request in audit logs -When you sign in and an SMS or voice MFA challenge is triggered, Microsoft can confirm the following steps given a Correlation ID and timestamp: +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a Reports Reader. +1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Audit logs**, and select the **Directory** tab. +1. Set the **Date range**, and add these filters: **Service: Azure MFA** and **Category: Authentication**. +1. Leave **Activity** set to **All** so you see both successful and failed requests. -1. **Request received.** Microsoft Entra generates the MFA request and constructs the payload for the SMS or voice request with the expected Microsoft or company branding. -1. **Provider selected.** Microsoft sends the request to one of multiple external third-party telecom providers matching your country code. -1. **Channel matched.** The request is routed through the correct channel (SMS or voice) per your configuration, selection, and policy requirements. -1. **Delivery confirmed.** The provider confirms receipt of the telecom request and marks it as successfully delivered with no alterations. +:::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Audit logs filtered by Service Azure MFA and Category Authentication, showing CyotDeliverySucceeded and CyotDeliveryFailed activities." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png"::: -After the provider confirms delivery, the request enters external telecom networks where Microsoft doesn't have direct visibility. Common causes include: +## Check sign-in logs -- **Device-level configuration.** Even when all steps to send the message are correct, the device itself could refuse the call or route it to voicemail. Microsoft automatically retries these failures across different providers. -- **Carrier-level blocking.** The carrier might block the call or message due to international automated fraud detection systems. -- **Regional availability issues.** In rare cases, the message is dropped due to availability issues in a specific country. Microsoft and its providers have robust retry and reroute mechanisms for these scenarios and post automated outage communications when the impact is broadly reported. +Use sign-in logs to confirm whether the user completed authentication. -### The call or message is altered by a downstream carrier +1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. +1. Find the sign-in by user and time, and open it. +1. On **Authentication Details**, review the method, whether the step succeeded, and the result detail. -Because the provider already confirmed delivery, Microsoft can only see a successful delivery per its specification. When message content is altered: +Sign-in logs show the method as **Text message** or **Voice**. To confirm that the request was sent through your provider, use audit logs. -- The customer should provide evidence that the message received on their device didn't appear with the expected branding or channel. -- Microsoft collaborates with the provider to understand the end-carrier behavior taken on behalf of the request. -- The provider will likely correct the route for the affected country code or phone number to avoid carriers that aren't honoring the original message contract. + + -## What to expect during an investigation +## Check Function App logs -Due to the complexity of global telecom routing and limited visibility beyond the provider, telecom delivery investigations involve coordination across multiple companies and stakeholders. +Use your Function App logs to see how your endpoint processed the request and what it returned to Microsoft Entra. -### Timeline +1. In the Azure portal, open the Function App created by setup. +1. Go to **Monitoring** > **Application Insights**, and open the linked Application Insights resource. +1. Select **Logs**, and run the following query for the time of the attempt: -Investigations into downstream customer-reported delivery issues can take 4–6 weeks. The provider checks their logs and, if no issue is found locally, queries downstream partners who might use additional providers. + ```kusto + AppRequests + | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) + | where Url has "/api/SendOtp" + | project TimeGenerated, ResultCode, Success, DurationMs, OperationId + | order by TimeGenerated desc + ``` -### Root cause analysis (RCA) policy +`ResultCode` shows what your Function App returned to Microsoft Entra. Carriers often don't share root cause details with Microsoft due to international visibility and competitive agreements. + + + + + + + + + + + + + -## Help with the investigation +## Identify who can help -To help Microsoft Support investigate provider-related issues: +Use what you see in audit logs to find the right contact. -- **Submit a Correlation ID and timestamp** for the sign-ins that need investigation. You can find these values in the [sign-in logs](~/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-ins.md). The Correlation ID returns all Request IDs associated with the sign-in. +| What you see | What to check | Contact | +|---|---|---| +| No CYOT activity in audit logs | Confirm the date range and filters, that the user is included in SMS or voice targeting, and that a new phone challenge was required. | Microsoft support | +| Only `CyotEvaluation` activity | The profile is in **Evaluation**. Switch to **Production** to route traffic through your provider. | No support needed | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointClientError` | Your endpoint rejected the request. Check your Function App logs and authentication settings. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointServerError` | Your endpoint returned an error or didn't respond in time. Check your Function App logs and your provider's status. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `NonceMismatch` | Your endpoint's response didn't match what Microsoft Entra expects. Compare any customizations with the CYOT sample. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliverySucceeded`, but the user didn't receive the code | Your endpoint accepted the request. Check your provider's delivery records. | Your telecom provider | +| The user received the code, but sign-in failed | Check the sign-in logs for an expired, reused, or incorrect code. | Microsoft support | +| Delivery blocked to certain countries/regions, fraud blocks, or unexpected charges | Review your provider's fraud, destination, and spending controls. | Your telecom provider | - To view the sign-in logs from the Microsoft Entra admin center: +> [!TIP] +> When a request times out, check your provider's records before you try again. Your provider might have already accepted the original request. - 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Reports Reader](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader). - 1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. + + - :::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png" alt-text="Screenshot that shows the Date and Correlation ID fields in the sign-in logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png"::: +## Contact support -- **Provide fresh samples.** End carriers often require Correlation IDs from the last 48–72 hours. It explains how telecom delivery works behind the scenes, what Microsoft can and can't see, and what to expect during an investigation. - - - +## Move to modern, phishing-resistant authentication -Use this article to trace SMS and voice requests end to end with Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), find where a request stopped, and contact the right team to resolve it: Microsoft support, your Azure team, or your telecom provider. +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Microsoft is committed to helping organizations adopt modern, phishing-resistant authentication methods. These providers rely on their own networks of suppliers, who control the routes for SMS and voice calls through local end-carrier networks. This supply chain represents thousands of individual carriers and routes around the globe. -Each request passes through four stages, and each stage is recorded in its own logs: +Microsoft maintains robust processes to help ensure successful delivery of every SMS and voice MFA request. However, once a request leaves the Microsoft network, delivery is delegated to external telecom providers. -| Stage | What happens | Where to look | -|---|---|---| -| 1. Microsoft Entra sends the request | Microsoft Entra requires an SMS or voice code and sends the request to your endpoint. | Microsoft Entra audit logs | -| 2. Your endpoint processes it | Your Function App receives the request and sends it to your telecom provider. | Function App logs | -| 3. Your provider delivers it | Your provider sends the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | Your provider's portal | -| 4. The user signs in | The user enters the code, and Microsoft Entra completes authentication. | Microsoft Entra sign-in logs | +These providers often share the same end routes and carriers in a given destination country/region but might operate under different contractual agreements or traffic priorities.
