Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a Reports Reader. -1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Audit logs**, and select the **Directory** tab. -1. Set the **Date range**, and add these filters: **Service: Azure MFA** and **Category: Authentication**. -1. Leave **Activity** set to **All** so you see both successful and failed requests. +When you sign in and an SMS or voice MFA challenge is triggered, Microsoft can confirm the following steps given a Correlation ID and timestamp: -:::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Audit logs filtered by Service Azure MFA and Category Authentication, showing CyotDeliverySucceeded and CyotDeliveryFailed activities." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png"::: +1. **Request received.** Microsoft Entra generates the MFA request and constructs the payload for the SMS or voice request with the expected Microsoft or company branding. +1. **Provider selected.** Microsoft sends the request to one of multiple external third-party telecom providers matching your country code. +1. **Channel matched.** The request is routed through the correct channel (SMS or voice) per your configuration, selection, and policy requirements. +1. **Delivery confirmed.** The provider confirms receipt of the telecom request and marks it as successfully delivered with no alterations. -Select the request to open **Audit Log Details**, and note these values: +After the provider confirms delivery, the request enters external telecom networks where Microsoft doesn't have direct visibility. Problems that occur beyond this point require collaboration with the provider to investigate. -| Field | What it tells you | -|---|---| -| Activity Type | `CyotDeliverySucceeded` means your endpoint accepted the request. `CyotDeliveryFailed` means it didn't complete. | -| DeliveryMethod | `Cyot` for a live request through your provider. `CyotEvaluation` for an evaluation request. | -| Channel | `Sms` or `Voice`. | -| AuthenticationMethod | The method used, such as `OneWaySms` or `OneWayVoiceMobileOtp`. | -| Correlation ID | The identifier to share with support. | -| FailureReason | Why a failed request didn't complete. | +## What can go wrong after delivery to the provider -:::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-log-details.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Audit Log Details for CyotDeliverySucceeded with DeliveryMethod Cyot and Channel Voice." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-log-details.png"::: +After the request reaches an external telecom provider, two types of problems can occur. - +### The call or message is dropped or blocked -## Check sign-in logs +The provider should confirm this issue to Microsoft. Common causes include: -Use sign-in logs to confirm whether the user completed authentication. +- **Device-level configuration.** Even when all steps to send the message are correct, the device itself could refuse the call or route it to voicemail. Microsoft automatically retries these failures across different providers. +- **Carrier-level blocking.** The carrier might block the call or message due to international automated fraud detection systems. +- **Regional availability issues.** In rare cases, the message is dropped due to availability issues in a specific country/region. Microsoft and its providers have robust retry and reroute mechanisms for these scenarios and post automated outage communications when the impact is broadly reported. -1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. -1. Find the sign-in by user and time, and open it. -1. On **Authentication Details**, review the method, whether the step succeeded, and the result detail. +### The call or message is altered by a downstream carrier -Sign-in logs show the method as **Text message** or **Voice**. To confirm that the request was sent through your provider, use audit logs. +Because the provider already confirmed delivery, Microsoft can only see a successful delivery per its specification. When message content is altered: - - +- The customer should provide evidence that the message received on their device didn't appear with the expected branding or channel. +- Microsoft collaborates with the provider to understand the end-carrier behavior taken on behalf of the request. +- The provider will likely correct the route for the affected country code or phone number to avoid carriers that aren't honoring the original message contract. -## Check Function App logs +## What to expect during an investigation -Use your Function App logs to see how your endpoint processed the request and what it returned to Microsoft Entra. +Due to the complexity of global telecom routing and limited visibility beyond the provider, telecom delivery investigations involve coordination across multiple companies and stakeholders. -1. In the Azure portal, open the Function App created by setup. -1. Go to **Monitoring** > **Application Insights**, and open the linked Application Insights resource. -1. Select **Logs**, and run the following query for the time of the attempt: +### Timeline - ```kusto - AppRequests - | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) - | where Url has "/api/SendOtp" - | project TimeGenerated, ResultCode, Success, DurationMs, OperationId - | order by TimeGenerated desc - ``` +Investigations into downstream customer-reported delivery issues can take 4–6 weeks. The provider checks their logs and, if no issue is found locally, queries downstream partners who might use additional providers. -`ResultCode` shows what your Function App returned to Microsoft Entra. To see your provider's response for the same request, query `AppTraces` with its `OperationId`. +### Root cause analysis (RCA) policy - - - - - - - - - - - - - +Microsoft doesn't publish RCAs for issues that originate with external telecom providers. Carriers often don't share root cause details with Microsoft due to international visibility and competitive agreements. -## Identify who can help +## Help with the investigation -Use what you see in audit logs to find the right contact. +To help Microsoft Support investigate provider-related issues: -| What you see | What to check | Contact | -|---|---|---| -| No CYOT activity in audit logs | Confirm the date range and filters, that the user is included in SMS or voice targeting, and that a new phone challenge was required. | Microsoft support | -| Only `CyotEvaluation` activity | The profile is in **Evaluation**. Switch to **Production** to route traffic through your provider. | No support needed | -| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointClientError` | Your endpoint rejected the request. Check your Function App logs and authentication settings. | Your Azure team | -| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointServerError` | Your endpoint returned an error or didn't respond in time. Check your Function App logs and your provider's status. | Your Azure team | -| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `NonceMismatch` | Your endpoint's response didn't match what Microsoft Entra expects. Compare any customizations with the CYOT sample. | Your Azure team | -| `CyotDeliverySucceeded`, but the user didn't receive the code | Your endpoint accepted the request. Check your provider's delivery records. | Your telecom provider | -| The user received the code, but sign-in failed | Check the sign-in logs for an expired, reused, or incorrect code. | Microsoft support | -| Delivery blocked to certain countries/regions, fraud blocks, or unexpected charges | Review your provider's fraud, destination, and spending controls. | Your telecom provider | +- **Submit a Correlation ID and timestamp** for the sign-ins that need investigation. You can find these values in the [sign-in logs](~/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-ins.md). The Correlation ID returns all Request IDs associated with the sign-in. -> [!TIP] -> When a request times out, check your provider's records before you try again. Your provider might have already accepted the original request. + To view the sign-in logs from the Microsoft Entra admin center: - - + 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Reports Reader](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader). + 1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. -## Contact support + :::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png" alt-text="Screenshot that shows the Date and Correlation ID fields in the sign-in logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png"::: -| Contact | Covers | How to reach | -|---|---|---| -| Microsoft support | Authentication method policy, Microsoft Entra authentication, and the request to your endpoint | [Get support for Microsoft Entra](/entra/fundamentals/how-to-get-support) | -| Your Azure team | Your Function App, its configuration, and Azure resources | Internal. messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Choose your own telephony provider now generally available
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Entra ID now generally supports Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) for SMS and voice authentication, retiring Microsoft-provided services by February 1, 2027. Organizations must select a provider, set up CYOT, and transition before that date, while Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant methods like passkeys.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated this post with additional information as the feature is now generally available. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) is now generally available in Microsoft Entra ID. With CYOT, your organization can deliver SMS and voice authentication through a supported telecom provider of its choice. You purchase the provider's offer in Microsoft Security Store and manage the commercial relationship directly with the provider. 

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication begins retiring on February 1, 2027. To keep SMS and voice authentication available for users who need it, set up CYOT before that date. 

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice. Use telephony-based authentication only for users who have a business, regulatory, or technical need for it.

What you need to do

If your organization plans to use CYOT: 

  1. Identify users who need SMS or voice. Confirm which users have a requirement that phishing-resistant methods can't meet. 
  2. Choose a provider. Compare the supported telecom providers on coverage, channels, pricing, support, and compliance. 
  3. Check purchasing requirements. Confirm that you have a paid Azure subscription that is eligible for Security Store purchases, and that you have the Owner role, or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator. 
  4. Estimate costs. Review provider pricing and Azure hosting costs. 
  5. Set up and roll out. Follow Set up SMS and voice. Start in evaluation mode, then increase traffic to your provider in stages. 
  6. Complete your transition before February 1, 2027. Review the guidance for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication.

Learn more 

  • Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication 
  • Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider 
  • Troubleshoot SMS and voice 
  • Protect against telephony fraud 
  • Plan for resiliency and high availability 
  • Frequently asked questions 
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication

englishSummary.overview: Today's report includes 6 new, 17 updated, and 0 removed Microsoft Entra documentation files across 5 documentation areas.

groups.title: identity/authentication
groups.summary: A new article explains how to configure telecom-provider fraud, destination, channel, spending, and alert controls; secure the CYOT integration; monitor activity; and respond to suspected fraud. The documentation explains CYOT delivery dependencies and resiliency approaches, including multi-region Azure Front Door deployments, secondary telecom providers, failover testing, capacity planning, and associated costs. The new guide explains how to connect Microsoft Entra SMS and voice authentication to a telecom provider using CYOT, including purchasing, Azure deployment, permissions, policy configuration, testing, and rollout. The documentation explains how to trace Choose Your Own Telephony Pro

groups.title: id-governance
groups.summary: Microsoft Entra ID Governance now supports reviewing access packages as single items in catalog access reviews. Reviewers can approve or deny each package; denial removes the assignment and all resources granted through it at the review end date. The documentation no longer includes the note that nested group drift is excluded and that reports compare assignments with users directly assigned to a group. The Agent ID default inactivity policy page updates links to related lifecycle policy and end-user agent management documentation. The documentation now states that catalog access reviews support access packages in preview and links to additional guidance.

groups.title: identity-platform
groups.summary: The documentation now covers using the Microsoft Entra External ID credential management API to let signed-in customers list, register, and delete passkeys, including setup, permissions, authentication, and endpoint details.

groups.title: external-id
groups.summary: The custom policies guidance now includes a screenshot of the Migration Policy Analyzer UI and updated author metadata. The documentation now points to the credential management API for signed-in customers to list, register, and delete their own passkeys with delegated permissions. It also adds a sample and warns that its deletion flow is for test tenants only. The JavaScript, React, and single-page application entries now link to “List and register passkeys” GitHub samples instead of the previous passkey samples.

groups.title: global-secure-access
groups.summary: The configuration guide no longer includes the note that a special Entra Admin Center link might be needed during the September 2026 rollout to view custom header details in Global Secure Access traffic logs. The documentation now lists Universal CAE’s supported device-based signals without the “preview” label.
